title: Fourier Weight of the Optimality Function
statement: For each natural number $q$, set $p_q=1/(q+2)$ and let $t_q$ be the standard Gaussian upper-tail quantile with tail probability $p_q$. Choose a dimension $d_q$ for which the indicator $A_q$ of the event that the normalized sum of the $d_q$ Boolean coordinates exceeds $t_q$ has mean within $p_q/2$ of $p_q$ and level-one Fourier weight within half the square of the Gaussian density at $t_q$ of that squared density. Let $F_q$ on the $(d_q+1)$-dimensional cube equal the first coordinate when the remaining coordinates are outside this event, and equal $1$ when they are inside it. Then $F_q$ has level-one Fourier weight $(1-\mathbb{E}A_q)^2+W_1(A_q)$.
caveat: The statement uses a dimension selected by an existence theorem; the prose spells out that selection and the associated functions.
